vision_summary.summary: The Vision document describes a hackathon MVP for a MEL (Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning) Agent for FarmerChat. FarmerChat is Digital Green's AI advisory assistant for small-scale farmers. The agent reads English insights that FarmerChat's insight extractor already stores for each farmer. It then generates short, tap-based follow-up surveys about the specific advice that farmer received. Each survey gets a send window from the crop calendar and the advice's action window, and is handed to a scheduler and broadcaster. The scope is Bihar, India, rabi season (November to March), with synthetic data, a simulated app and simulated delivery. Quality and timeliness matter more than scale. Quality must be shown through evaluation against a Digital Green golden dataset, with at least one improvement iteration. The agent must check its own output before scheduling, and must generate nothing when an insight does not support a meaningful question. Safety is a standing requirement: no personal information requested, no new or contradictory agronomic advice, and negative answers routed for follow-up. RCTs (Randomized Controlled Trials) remain the verification method.
source_facts: [Executive Summary] Goal: a MEL Agent that reads FarmerChat insights and generates short, personalized follow-up surveys timed to the crop calendar, handed to a scheduler and broadcaster. Proven by evaluations against a Digital Green golden dataset, for Bihar farmers, November to March. Digital Green intends a pilot with around 10,000 farmers if quality holds.

[FarmerChat Today] FarmerChat serves around 2.2 million farmers by text, voice or photo. It runs on AWS with memory and around 20 MCP servers, including AgMCP. The query path is alignment agent, main agent, then insight extractor. Resolution types: direct action, indirect action, wait and watch. Insights are stored in English. Agents return JSON that the app renders as UI.
[The Background Agent Vision] NightSync, SeasonPlanner and FarmWatch are future phases. The MEL Agent is the hackathon focus.
[Problem Statement] Field surveys and RCTs are expensive and do not scale. Earlier digital and voice surveys were broadcast and generic. Irrelevant questions cost farmer trust.

[Business Drivers] Drivers: adoption data at scale, context already exists, timeliness, trust (quality over reach). RCTs stay as the verifier. The source claims a working system would be a first for the development sector.

[Target Users and Stakeholders] Users: small-scale farmers in Bihar (mobile app, voice in future), the Digital Green MEL team, the Digital Green product and AI team, and an external evaluation agency that needs consistent, auditable data collection.

[Business Constraints] Quality and timeliness, not infrastructure. Do not bombard farmers. Synthetic data only (fully synthetic, not anonymized). Contract first: REST API plus JSON survey object. All outputs open source.

[Core Concepts] Defines insight, contextual survey, survey item (one tap question with fixed options), survey schedule (send window), broadcaster, agent-to-UI JSON, and golden dataset. FarmerChat is not available at the hackathon.

[Design Principles] One farmer, one context. Short and tappable. Ask at the right time. Quality before volume (a missed survey beats an irrelevant one). Evaluate before scheduling (schema, relevance, language). Contract over framework. Language is a BCP 47 parameter (for example hi-IN, en-IN).

[Safety Tenet] Never collect personal information through a survey. Do not give new agronomic advice or contradict the advice received. Answers suggesting the advice failed or the crop was damaged should be routed back for follow-up, not only recorded.

[MVP Success Criteria] Ingest about 5,000 to 10,000 synthetic insights for 200 to 500 farmers. Generate valid JSON per eligible insight that references the specific advice and resolution. Send window consistent with crop calendar and action window. Score against the golden dataset for relevance, timeliness and format. Measure generation time per survey and per dataset. Scheduler orders by send window with a per-farmer frequency cap. Broadcaster stub delivers to a simulated tap app. Failed surveys are not scheduled. English end to end; Hindi via hi-IN.

[Features In Scope (MVP)] Must Have: insight ingestion, survey generation agent, survey JSON contract, self-evaluation step (schema plus relevance), evaluation harness (repeated runs), survey scheduler. Should Have: broadcaster stub and simulated app, Hindi surveys, latency and cost telemetry. Exploratory: response write-back, negative-outcome follow-up, alternative channels.

[Features Explicitly Out of Scope (MVP)] Out of scope: other background agents, production integration, real delivery, AgMCP and live external data, other languages, other regions, replacing RCTs, delivery at scale.

[MVP User Journeys] Journey 1: Hindi aphid question on mustard, direct action within two days if no rain; a three-item Hindi survey; send window five to seven days after the advice, after a weekly survey check. Journey 2: the MEL team runs the full dataset, scores, adjusts and reruns. Journey 3 (stretch): a negative answer is written back and a follow-up case is created.

[MVP Definition of Done] All Must Have features implemented and tested. Full dataset run. Golden-dataset scores with at least one improvement iteration. Time per survey and per batch reported. Invalid or low-scoring surveys verified not scheduled. Schema validation. Code, IaC, evaluation harness and README published open source.

[Key Risks] Risks: scope may be too small for 2 to 2.5 days; late data (mitigation: agree schema, generate a small sample); Hindi quality hard to judge; JSON mismatch with the Digital Green format (agree schema before the event); farmer overload (frequency cap).
open_questions: [Open Questions] How many items per survey, and which tap question types work best?
[Open Questions] Which insights deserve a survey, and should several insights for one farmer be combined?
[Open Questions] How should the send window be derived when advice depends on weather?
[Open Questions] Which automatic checks (schema, rubric, LLM-as-judge) best predict golden-dataset and MEL reviewer acceptance?
[Open Questions] How can generation be batched or parallelized without losing quality?
[Open Questions] Stretch: how should answers become adoption and outcome measures comparable with RCT results?
Review question: what threshold defines 'low-scoring' for the Definition of Done? The source gives none.
Review question: what is the per-farmer frequency cap value? Journey 1 implies one survey per week but does not state a rule.
Review question: what does 'routed back for follow-up' target in a sandbox with no FarmerChat advice path?

technical_summary.summary: The Technical document sets the build environment. Quality, proven with evaluations, is the main goal; infrastructure and scale are secondary. FarmerChat, Digital Green AWS accounts and real data are not available. Teams use AWS Workshop Studio accounts with Python 3.12 or later. Google ADK is preferred, but Strands Agents or another framework is acceptable if the REST plus JSON contract is met. Amazon Bedrock is required, with the model kept behind an abstraction. Model tiering is suggested. Hosting may be AgentCore Runtime or containers (production is moving to Amazon EKS). If a database is used, use RDS for PostgreSQL or Aurora PostgreSQL. Evaluation is central: hill-climb against the golden dataset. Dimensions are relevance, timeliness, format, safety and speed. Deterministic checks cover format and timing, and a rubric-grounded LLM-as-judge covers relevance. The document gives draft insight, survey and response JSON contracts, a shared simulated clock with manual triggers, and a rule to deliver only to the simulated app.
source_facts: [Hackathon Approach and Expectations] Quality is the goal. FarmerChat is not available. Lean toward Google ADK but other frameworks are acceptable. Hosting is flexible (AgentCore or containers). No prescriptive UI: Streamlit or CLI is fine; voice is welcome. Use Amazon Bedrock with the model behind an abstraction.

[Project Technical Summary] Cloud runtime on AWS, built in AWS Workshop Studio hackathon accounts. Customer stack: Python with Google ADK, agent-to-agent REST, agent-to-UI JSON, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, production moving to Amazon EKS, open-source codebase DG_Open.
[Reference Architecture] Teams may simplify, for example a single process with a loop standing in for the scheduler. The diagram is an embedded image that is not available to this review.
[Required Languages] Python 3.12 or later for the agent, scheduler and evaluation harness.
[Permitted Languages] SQL (PostgreSQL) if a database is used.
[Agent Framework] Google ADK (production, model agnostic), Strands Agents SDK (native to Bedrock and AgentCore), or another framework if the contract is met.
[Suggested Libraries] Boto3 / Bedrock Runtime Converse API, Pydantic or JSON Schema, FastAPI, Streamlit, AWS CDK or Terraform.

[Models and AI Services] Amazon Bedrock is required. Enabled models must be confirmed with event staff. Tiering is worth exploring: a smaller model for eligibility and checks, a larger one for generation. Log tokens, estimated cost and time per survey and per batch.

[Evaluation and Quality Measurement] Hill-climb: run, score, change, rerun, show the trend. Dimensions: relevance, timeliness, format (valid JSON, tap items, item count within limits, correct language), safety (no new advice, no personal information), speed. Deterministic checks for format and timing. LLM-as-judge for relevance, grounded in an MEL rubric (confirm whether one exists). English is the baseline; Hindi is reviewed by people.

[Provided Datasets] Insights: about 5,000 to 10,000 rows, 200 to 500 Bihar farmers, rabi season, Hindi conversations, English insights. Golden dataset: insights with expected surveys. Crop calendar: from Digital Green or public references (confirm). All synthetic.

[Core Data Contracts (draft, to align with Digital Green's insight and agent-to-UI formats)] Insight fields include insight_id, farmer_id, created_at, conversation_language, location, crop, crop_stage, topic, query_summary, advice_summary, resolution_type, action_window_days. Survey fields include source_insight_ids, language, send_window (not_before, not_after), items (single_choice with options), rationale, self_eval (schema_valid, relevance_score). Response fields include answers by item_id and option_id, and answered_at. The example prompts are English for readability.
[Simulated Clock] The scheduler and broadcaster read a shared simulated clock so the demo can move through the season in minutes. Every scheduled step has a manual trigger.
[Cloud Environment] One Workshop Studio account per team. Region: wherever the required Bedrock models are enabled (confirm).

[Infrastructure Preferences] AgentCore Runtime or containers are acceptable; containers ease a later move to EKS. Use RDS for PostgreSQL or Aurora PostgreSQL if a database is needed. Do not send real messages; deliver to the simulated app only.

independent_options.title: Evaluation-first generation core with hill-climb run log
independent_options.purpose: Build the smallest generator that emits contract-valid surveys from insights, and score it against the golden dataset across repeated runs. Evaluation is treated as the mandatory baseline, not as a differentiator.
source_support: Vision: MVP Success Criteria (scored against golden dataset for relevance, timeliness, format)
Vision: MVP Definition of Done (at least one improvement iteration shown)
Vision: Features In Scope (MVP) (survey generation agent, survey JSON contract, evaluation harness: Must Have)
Technical: Evaluation and Quality Measurement (hill-climb; deterministic checks plus LLM-as-judge)
Technical: Core Data Contracts (draft, to align with Digital Green's insight and agent-to-UI formats)
Technical: Models and AI Services (Bedrock required; model behind an abstraction)
independent_options.scope: Source fact: ingestion, generation, schema, and evaluation harness are Must Have. Scope: load insights; generate a survey per insight through Bedrock Converse; validate with Pydantic; score format and timing deterministically; score relevance with an LLM-as-judge; save each run with its prompt version.
independent_options.proposed_extension: Proposed: a run manifest that records prompt version, model ID, and per-dimension scores, plus a per-run comparison table so the hill-climb trend is visible. The model ID sits behind a thin provider interface.

aws_mapping.requirement: Mandatory per Technical. Confirm enabled models and region with event staff.

aws_mapping.role: Store run manifests, generated surveys, and score files
aws_mapping.requirement: Optional. Confirm availability in the Workshop Studio account. Local files are an acceptable fallback.

workflow: Load insights and the golden dataset; join on an agreed key.
Generate a survey JSON per insight via the model abstraction.
Validate against the Pydantic schema; record failures.
Run deterministic format and timing checks.
Run a rubric-grounded LLM-as-judge for relevance.
Write the run manifest; change the prompt; rerun; compare runs.
independent_options.minimum_demo: Two scored runs on the same golden subset, with different prompt versions, side by side, plus one valid survey JSON shown next to its source insight.
dependencies: Agreed join key between golden and generated surveys
risks: An LLM-as-judge may not match MEL reviewer judgement (source Open Question).
Without a rubric, relevance scores are hard to defend.
The improvement shown may come from noise unless the run setup is held constant.
Hindi cannot be scored automatically against the English baseline.
independent_options.completion_check: At least two runs are recorded with per-dimension scores against the golden dataset, and every scored survey passes or is flagged by schema validation.
independent_options.one_day_cuts: Run on a golden subset first. Defer full-dataset runs, S3, and dashboards. Keep the judge prompt simple and documented.

independent_options.title: Eligibility gate and tiered models (abstain when no meaningful question)
independent_options.purpose: Make 'quality before volume' explicit: decide per insight whether a survey is warranted, and log the abstain reason. Explore the suggested small-model and large-model tiering.
source_support: Vision: Design Principles (Quality before volume: generate nothing if the insight does not support a meaningful question)
Vision: Open Questions (Which insights deserve a survey at all; should several insights be combined?)
Vision: MVP Success Criteria ('For each eligible insight')
Technical: Models and AI Services (tiering: smaller model for eligibility and checks, larger for generation)
Technical: Evaluation and Quality Measurement (Speed: time per survey and for the full dataset)
independent_options.scope: Source fact: eligibility is implied but not defined. Scope: a gate step before generation that returns eligible or not eligible with a reason code; optional grouping of insights per farmer; token and time logging per step.
independent_options.proposed_extension: Proposed: a reason-code list (for example, a missing advice summary, or the outcome not observable in the season) as a reviewable artifact for the MEL team. Proposed: compare gate decisions with golden dataset coverage, if the golden set implies which insights get surveys.

aws_mapping.role: Smaller model for eligibility, larger model for generation
aws_mapping.requirement: Mandatory per Technical. Which tier models are enabled must be confirmed.

aws_mapping.role: Optional logs and metrics for tokens and latency per step
aws_mapping.requirement: Optional. Confirm account permissions. Local logs are an acceptable fallback.

inputs: Golden dataset (to infer expected eligibility, if possible)
workflow: Apply cheap deterministic pre-filters on the fields present.
Call the small model for an eligibility decision plus a reason code.
Send eligible insights to the generation model.
Log tokens, estimated cost, and time per step.
Report abstain counts by reason and compare with the golden data.
independent_options.minimum_demo: A small batch where some insights are skipped with visible reason codes, the rest produce surveys, and per-step tokens and time are shown.
dependencies: Two suitable Bedrock models enabled, or one model used for both tiers
Golden dataset signals about which insights should be surveyed
risks: Eligibility criteria are not defined in the sources and may not match MEL intent.
Combining insights per farmer complicates golden-dataset scoring.
independent_options.completion_check: Every processed insight has either a generated survey or a logged reason code, and the step-level token and time logs are produced.
independent_options.one_day_cuts: Use one model for both tiers if only one is available. Skip multi-insight grouping. Use deterministic pre-filters only if model calls are constrained.

independent_options.title: Deterministic send-window scheduler, simulated clock, broadcaster stub and tap app
independent_options.purpose: Show timeliness and non-bombardment end to end: send windows from the crop calendar and action window, a per-farmer frequency cap, and delivery to a simulated app on a simulated clock.
source_support: Vision: Features In Scope (MVP) (survey scheduler: Must Have; broadcaster stub and simulated app: Should Have)
Vision: MVP Success Criteria (scheduler orders by send window, per-farmer cap, broadcaster stub to simulated app)
Vision: MVP User Journeys (Journey 1: send window five to seven days after advice, weekly check)
Technical: Simulated Clock (shared clock; manual trigger for every step)
Technical: Reference Architecture (single process with a loop may stand in for the scheduler)
Technical: Infrastructure Preferences (deliver to the simulated app only)
independent_options.scope: Source fact: the scheduler is Must Have; the broadcaster and app are Should Have but appear in the Success Criteria. Scope: compute send_window deterministically; order surveys; apply the cap; advance the clock; deliver due surveys to a Streamlit or CLI tap view; record taps locally.
independent_options.proposed_extension: Proposed: send-window rules keyed on resolution_type and action_window_days, with a visible explanation per survey. Weather-dependent advice is labeled as an unresolved rule (source Open Question), not guessed. The cap value is a configurable parameter, not a fixed number.

aws_mapping.role: Upstream generation only; the scheduler itself is deterministic
aws_mapping.requirement: Mandatory for the agent per Technical.

aws_mapping.service: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL or Aurora PostgreSQL
aws_mapping.role: Optional store for surveys, schedule, and responses
aws_mapping.requirement: Optional. The Technical document prefers it if a database is used. Confirm account availability. In-memory or local storage is acceptable for a simplified demo.

workflow: Compute send_window per survey from the calendar and action window.
Detect cap conflicts per farmer; defer or drop by rule.
Advance the simulated clock or use a manual trigger.
The broadcaster stub picks up due surveys.
The simulated app renders single_choice items and records taps.
independent_options.minimum_demo: Advance the clock across part of the season and show surveys appearing only inside their windows. Show one farmer's second survey deferred by the cap, and record a tap answer in the simulated app.
dependencies: Survey fixtures if generation is not ready
risks: Weather-dependent windows have no defined rule in the sources.
Cap conflict policy (defer, merge, or drop) is unspecified.
UI work can absorb time that evaluation needs.
independent_options.completion_check: Every scheduled survey has a send_window that a deterministic check confirms; no farmer exceeds the configured cap; delivery happens only on the simulated clock to the simulated app.
independent_options.one_day_cuts: Use a CLI instead of Streamlit, in-memory storage instead of RDS, a single-process loop, and a manual clock trigger only.

independent_options.purpose: Expose the agent through a clean REST and JSON contract that matches the draft schemas, so the integration point is demonstrable regardless of framework.
source_support: Vision: Business Constraints (Contract first: REST API and JSON survey object)
Vision: Design Principles (Contract over framework; language is a BCP 47 parameter)
Vision: Key Risks (Survey JSON may not match the agent-to-UI format; agree schema early)
Technical: Hackathon Approach and Expectations (hosting flexible: AgentCore or containers)
Technical: Suggested Libraries (FastAPI, Pydantic, AWS CDK or Terraform)
Technical: Core Data Contracts (draft, to align with Digital Green's insight and agent-to-UI formats)

independent_options.proposed_extension: Proposed: contract tests that validate request and response bodies against the published schema, and a schema version field so mismatches with Digital Green's agent-to-UI format are detectable later.

aws_mapping.requirement: Optional. Confirm availability in the account and region.

inputs: Draft insight, survey, and response schemas
workflow: Define Pydantic models from the draft contracts.
Export JSON Schema.
Implement endpoints that call the generator.
Add contract tests.
Deploy one path, or run locally if deployment is blocked.
independent_options.minimum_demo: Call the generate endpoint with a synthetic insight and language en-IN, then hi-IN, and show both responses validating against the published schema.
dependencies: Schema agreement with Digital Green (Key Risks)

Hindi output still needs human review.

independent_options.one_day_cuts: Run locally with documented IaC as a stretch. Expose only the generate endpoint. Skip auth beyond what the event requires.

independent_options.title: Safety checks, response write-back, and negative-outcome flagging (simulated)
independent_options.purpose: Turn the Safety Tenet into checkable gates: no personal information requested, no new or contradictory advice. Close the loop on synthetic responses by flagging negative outcomes for follow-up without generating advice.
source_support: Vision: Safety Tenet (no personal information; no new advice; route negative responses back)
Vision: Features In Scope (MVP) (response write-back and negative-outcome follow-up: Exploratory)
Vision: MVP User Journeys ((Stretch) Journey 3: a negative answer triggers follow-up)
Technical: Evaluation and Quality Measurement (Safety: no new advice, no personal information requested)
Technical: Core Data Contracts (response object)
independent_options.scope: Source fact: safety is a standing requirement and an evaluation dimension; write-back and follow-up are Exploratory. Scope: a pre-schedule safety check on each survey; storing synthetic tap responses against survey and insight; a rule that marks negative-outcome options as follow-up cases in a simulated queue.
independent_options.proposed_extension: Proposed: option-level tags in the survey (for example, a flag on 'not reduced' or 'crop damaged') so negative-outcome detection is deterministic, not model-inferred. The follow-up case only records a referral; it does not generate advice.

aws_mapping.role: LLM check for new or contradictory advice relative to advice_summary
Optional extra screen for personal-information requests in generated prompts
aws_mapping.requirement: Optional. Confirm availability and region. Do not rely on it alone.
Optional. Confirm availability. A local list is an acceptable fallback. No real messages to anyone.

inputs: Synthetic responses from the simulated app
workflow: Run the safety check on each survey before scheduling; block failures.
Record taps from the simulated app as response objects.
Detect tagged negative options.
Create a simulated follow-up case referencing the insight.
Report counts of blocked surveys and flagged responses.
independent_options.minimum_demo: One survey blocked for asking a personal question or adding advice, and one synthetic negative answer that produces a follow-up case record with no advice text.
dependencies: Agreement on what counts as a negative outcome
risks: Safety checks can produce false positives and false negatives.
The real follow-up path into FarmerChat does not exist here (Journey 3 depends on that contract).
Responses are self-reports; they indicate reported adoption, not causal impact.
independent_options.completion_check: Surveys that fail the safety check are verified not scheduled, and each tagged negative response produces exactly one follow-up record.
independent_options.one_day_cuts: Fold the safety check into the OPT-1 evaluation as a dimension. Use fixtures instead of live taps. Skip Guardrails and SQS.

recommended_approach: Recommendation for the architect's consideration, not a decision. Treat OPT-1 as the baseline because the evaluation harness, generation, contract, and self-evaluation are Must Have, and evaluation is mandatory, not a differentiator. Then choose one further slice according to team strength and data readiness. OPT-3 covers the Must Have scheduler and makes timeliness visible. OPT-2 best expresses 'quality before volume'. Fold the deterministic safety checks from OPT-5 into the OPT-1 evaluation as a cheap dimension. Wrap the generator with the OPT-4 contract endpoint late, run locally if deployment is blocked. Defer write-back, follow-up queues, voice, and full AWS deployment unless the baseline is stable. Confirm Bedrock model access, region, golden dataset format, rubric existence, and crop calendar source before committing to any slice.
source_tensions: Vision Features In Scope (MVP) marks the broadcaster stub and simulated app as Should Have, but MVP Success Criteria require a broadcaster stub delivering to a simulated app.
Vision Features In Scope (MVP) marks Hindi surveys as Should Have, but MVP Success Criteria require Hindi output when passed hi-IN.
Vision Features In Scope (MVP) marks latency and cost telemetry as Should Have, but MVP Success Criteria and MVP Definition of Done require generation time per survey and per batch.

Vision Safety Tenet says negative responses should be routed back for follow-up as a standing requirement, but Features In Scope (MVP) marks negative-outcome follow-up as Exploratory and MVP User Journeys labels it a stretch.

The self-evaluation step is 'schema validation plus a relevance check' in Features In Scope (MVP), but Design Principles add language; Technical Evaluation and Quality Measurement adds safety and speed as dimensions.
Vision MVP Success Criteria score relevance, timeliness, and format; Technical Evaluation and Quality Measurement also lists safety and speed.
Vision Key Risks says scope may be too small for 2 to 2.5 days; the review context states one day remains.

Vision Business Drivers says the agent produces the same kind of insight an RCT would; the same section and Features Explicitly Out of Scope (MVP) keep RCTs as the verifier. Survey self-reports do not establish causality.

Vision Executive Summary cites a pilot of around 10,000 farmers; Business Constraints and Features Explicitly Out of Scope (MVP) refer to not proving delivery to 100,000 users. These are different numbers for different purposes.
Vision Key Risks says agree the schema before the event; Technical Core Data Contracts are still marked draft.
Vision MVP Definition of Done requires 'low-scoring' surveys not to be scheduled, but no scoring threshold is defined; the relevance_score value in the Technical example is illustrative only.
Technical Provided Datasets leaves the crop calendar source as 'Digital Green or public agronomy references (confirm)'; Vision MVP Success Criteria require send windows consistent with it.
caveats: This review used only the extracted text of the two documents. The reference architecture image, the datasets, any Workshop Studio account, the code repository, real FarmerChat, and any event rubric were not inspected.
No hour estimates, completion claims, or win claims are made. All options are candidates for discussion.

Amazon Bedrock is the only mandatory AWS service per the Technical document. All other AWS services listed are optional, and their availability in the account, region, and model catalogue must be checked.
All data is synthetic. All delivery is simulated. No real messages are sent to anyone.
No agronomic advice is added. Survey items must only ask about advice already given, and follow-up cases only record a referral.
Surveys must not request personal information.
Survey responses are self-reported adoption and outcome signals. They do not replace RCTs and do not establish causality.
Hindi quality cannot be confirmed automatically against the English baseline; the sources require review by Hindi-speaking participants and Digital Green.
Labels marked 'Source fact' restate the documents; labels marked 'Proposed' are this review's extensions and are not source requirements.

Terms: MEL = Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning; RCT = Randomized Controlled Trial; LLM-as-judge = a language model scoring output against a rubric; BCP 47 = standard language tag format such as hi-IN; hill-climb = repeated run, score, adjust cycles.
